transcript: Let's talk about previews on Broadway. You may have seen that wanted recently launched this preview pricing where for all of their weekday previews, all tickets in the balcony will be $50, all tickets in the mezzanine will be 80, and all tickets in the orchestra will be 100. Now, this is not only a really good deal, but also emblematic of how previews on Broadway used to work. Now, they didn't necessarily all use the same pricing scheme, where all tickets in a section were the same price. But traditionally, tickets for preview performances cost less money. And that is because it is still a preview. The show is still being developed. And for a lot of people, myself included, there is a thrill in that. Knowing that the show that you are about to see potentially will never exist again. Like I am one of the lucky people that got to see the threesome ballet in chess before it was cut after first preview. Not to mention that cheaper tickets during previews also just help get more people through the door in those early performances before reviews are out and so that you can start building your word of mouth. But in recent years, this whole notion of tickets being cheaper during previews has kind of gone out the window. In fact, the only other show that I've really noticed doing this is Paddington. If you look at Paddington's prices during previews, they start at $69 and go All the way up to 2:50, and post opening that goes up to $89. All the way up to 2 90. So post opening all tickets are going up anywhere from 20 to 40 dollars. And I do think it's worth pointing out that the two shows doing this are original musicals, and they don't have someone like a Rachel Zegler or a Tom Hiddleston to reliably sell those preview tickets out before they even start performances. And so I do think that this is an incredibly smart way to get people through the door early while also properly setting audience expectations that this is a preview. It might not be quite as polished, things might go wrong, but that's okay. That is what previews are for.
